contributions.statement: Before rolling out an agent workflow or harness that was tuned or searched on one task set (one repo's tickets, one content type), evaluate it on a structurally different split against an untuned baseline, because searched harnesses lost 25-30 points off-distribution and one fell below the untuned baseline.
contributions.evidence: §3.3: Meta-Harness-searched polyreason harness 72% in-distribution vs 47% cross-distribution; searched math harness 67% vs 37%, below the brief-only compile (39.6). The drop is partly selection on the in-distribution split, and there are no intervals; QA/reasoning workloads, not coding.

contributions.statement: Keep a tuned LLM workflow as a typed declarative description (step DAG, named branch signals, rules that pick model/parameters from those signals, prompt templates) with provenance, from which runnable code can be regenerated.
contributions.evidence: Table 2: recover-then-compile matched the original harness within ±0.011 accuracy and ±0.013 ¢/q on 100 questions (3 harnesses x 3 replicates per domain), for about $2.5 per round trip. Aggregate match only, with no per-question agreement.

reason: The paper's evaluation is self-described as preliminary, and its workloads are QA and reasoning, not coding. Keeping workflows declarative is established practice. The only refinement is a weak, selection-confounded caution that searched harnesses drop sharply off-distribution.
